content: 1. In many settings, it is not possible to collect key population-specific data through routine program monitoring. Surveys are required to gather this information. 2. The percentage of people living with HIV (PLHIV) who have been diagnosed and are aware of their HIV-positive status is calculated as follows: Numerator (N): The number of PLHIV who have been diagnosed and received their test results. Denominator (D): The total number of PLHIV. This data can be disaggregated by sex, age groups (<1, 1–4, 5–9, 10–19, 20–24, 25–49, 50+ years), key populations, and other target populations. 3. Surveys collecting HIV serostatus and asking whether respondents know their positive status are used to calculate the indicator as the proportion of PLHIV who report knowing their status. 4. In the absence of a direct question about awareness of HIV status, a plausible range and midpoint can be constructed based on: The higher value of either the percentage of PLHIV tested in the past 12 months who received their results or the percentage of all PLHIV in care (as the lower end of the range). The percentage of PLHIV ever tested (as the upper end of the range). Additional data sources, such as other surveys, program data, and modeled estimates, can be used to triangulate and refine these estimates. 5. Determining the proportion of PLHIV who know their HIV status is critical, as this knowledge serves as the entry point to the continuum of care. Disaggregated estimates can identify gaps in diagnosing PLHIV. 6. The proportion of PLHIV who know their HIV-positive status should also be globally reported for target populations where national indicators are collected, including: The percentage of key populations. The percentage of pregnant women tested in the past 12 months who know their status. 7. The number of people tested for HIV and who received their results within the past 12 months is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of people tested for HIV and who received their results within the past 12 months. Denominator (D): Not applicable for this indicator, but population size estimates can be used for generalized or concentrated epidemics. Data can be disaggregated by test result, sex, age (<1, 1–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19, 20–49, 50+ years), key populations, and other target populations. 8. Retesting for HIV within the past 12 months is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of people tested and who received their results more than once within the past 12 months. Denominator (D): Not applicable, but population size estimates can be used. Retesters can be categorized as: 1. Retesting due to ongoing risk. 2. Retesting after discrepant results. 3. Retesting to verify diagnosis. Program records should quantify the number of retesters and subtract them from the total number of testers to determine the number of unique individuals tested. Understanding the reasons for retesting can help explain retesting patterns. 9. The number of pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) or having facility-based deliveries who were tested for HIV during pregnancy or already knew their HIV-positive status is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of pregnant women tested for HIV during pregnancy or already aware of their HIV-positive status. Denominator (D): The number of pregnant women who delivered within the past 12 months (population-based) or attended ANC or had a facility-based delivery (program-based). HIV status/test results can be categorized as: 1. Known HIV infection at ANC entry. 2. Tested HIV-positive during current pregnancy. 3. Tested HIV-negative during current pregnancy. Total identified HIV-positive women = 1 + 2. Optional disaggregation includes pregnant women who inject drugs. 10. Early HIV testing of HIV-exposed infants born within the past 12 months is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of HIV-exposed infants tested for HIV within two months of birth. Denominator (D): The number of HIV-positive pregnant women who delivered within the past 12 months. Test results can be categorized as positive, negative, indeterminate, or other. Early virological testing of infants is critical for initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART) early in children with confirmed HIV infection and for counseling efforts to prevent seroconversion in those with a negative early test result. 11. Retesting to verify HIV diagnosis at ART initiation is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of PLHIV who initiated ART within the past 12 months and had a retest to verify HIV diagnosis. Denominator (D): The number of PLHIV who initiated ART within the past 12 months. This is a quality measure to assess whether retesting to verify HIV diagnosis at ART initiation is being conducted. 12. The percentage of new and relapsed tuberculosis (TB) patients with an HIV test result recorded in the TB register is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of new and relapsed TB patients registered during the reporting period who had an HIV test result recorded. Denominator (D): The number of new and relapsed TB patients registered during the reporting period. Data can be disaggregated by sex, age (0–4, 5–14, 15+), and HIV status (positive, negative, unknown). Knowing the HIV status of TB patients enables linking them to appropriate HIV services. 13. The percentage of key population respondents previously unaware of their HIV-positive status who were tested for HIV and received their results within the past 12 months is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of key population respondents previously unaware of their HIV-positive status who were tested and received their results. Denominator (D): The number of key population respondents in the survey. Key populations include men who have sex with men, people in prisons and other closed settings, people who inject drugs, sex workers, and transgender individuals. This indicator measures the program’s effectiveness in encouraging HIV testing as both a prevention tool and an entry point for early care and treatment. 14. The percentage of people who have tested for HIV using a self-test kit is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of people who have tested for HIV using a self-test kit. Denominator (D): The total number surveyed. Data can be disaggregated by specific populations of interest. 15. General annual HIV testing services (HTS) coverage is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of adult respondents tested for HIV within the past 12 months and who received their results. Denominator (D): The number of adult respondents (15 years and older). Data can be disaggregated by sex and age (15–19, 20–24, 25–49, 50+). This indicator measures the proportion of the general population covered by HTS services in the preceding 12 months, particularly relevant for generalized epidemics. 16. The percentage of HIV-positive adults receiving HIV care within the past 12 months whose sexual partner’s HIV status is documented is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of HIV-positive adults receiving HIV care whose sexual partner’s HIV status is documented. Denominator (D): The number of HIV-positive adults receiving HIV care who have a sexual partner. This indicator measures the program’s ability to identify and test the sexual partners of people receiving HIV care, aiming to prevent ongoing transmission in sero-discordant couples and enroll HIV-positive partners in care services. 17. The number of ART sites with quality improvement activities implemented in the last six months is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of ART sites with quality improvement activities addressing clinical HIV program processes or outcomes and with documented results. Denominator (D): The number of health facilities dispensing antiretrovirals (ARVs) in the last 12 months. This is a critical component of capacity building for quality service provision. 18. The number of HIV testing services (HTS) sites that experienced a stock-out of HIV diagnostic tests or reagents during a reporting period is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of HTS sites with a stock-out. Denominator (D): The number of reporting HTS sites. This indicator provides valuable information on trends in the availability of laboratory services but does not measure the adequacy of coverage or the quality, cost, or effectiveness of services provided. 19. The number of testing laboratories with satisfactory performance in external quality assessment (EQA) or proficiency testing (PT) is measured as follows: Numerator (N): The number of testing laboratories with satisfactory performance in EQA/PT. Denominator (D): The number of testing laboratories participating in EQA/PT. This indicator measures laboratory performance based on the accuracy and reliability of diagnostics, ensuring the validity of test results across the biomedical infrastructure. It also helps detect low performance and address weaknesses through supervision, verification, and upgrading of equipment and supplies.
